title: ORT env creation logs 'Init provider bridge failed.' in winml venv
head: 2724c4cd
stderr_excerpt: [W:onnxruntime:Default, onnxruntime_pybind_module.cc:45 onnxruntime::python::CreateOrtEnv] Init provider bridge failed.
impact: Unknown-but-bounded: all observed GPU executions succeed despite it; treated as warning-to-audit, not harmless-by-assumption.
observation: The warning is emitted once per process at onnxruntime import/env creation in .venv-winml, BEFORE any amdgpu-ep.dll registration and independent of it. Also seen in G1-era runs. GPU sessions still create and execute (canary cand[1] OK; G2/G3 32/32 receipts).
hypotheses: ORT python bridge tries to preload a provider bridge DLL that is absent in the windowsml distribution (cosmetic, no functional effect)
Bridge init failure disables some provider surface we have not used yet (e.g. direct AMDGPUExecutionProvider class registration)
next_discriminating_experiment: Fresh process: import onnxruntime with ORT log level verbose and capture which bridge init is attempted; compare providers surface with/without the warning. Bounded: 3 runs.

title: MIGraphX auto_save_problem_cache write fails (WindowsApps protected path)
head: 2724c4cd
exception: auto_save_problem_cache: save failed: write_buffer: Failure opening file: C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...\ExecutionProvider\problem_cache.json
impact: Possible slower session-create across processes; no execution or parity failure observed. Never modify WindowsApps/ACLs (forbidden).
observation: Emitted by the AMDGPU EP when a graph compiles in our process: the bundled MIGraphX attempts to persist its problem cache next to the MSIX DLL under WindowsApps, which is ACL-protected (read/execute for user). Emitted 3x during one canary session-create+run. Compilation and execution still succeed.
hypotheses: External root cause: MSIX package does not relocate its cache dir; expected user-writable path is not configured by this EP build (ep_options empty, no documented option on 1.8.65.0)
Consequence is cold-compile cost per process (no persistent cache), not correctness
next_discriminating_experiment: Measure session-create wall time in N=3 fresh processes vs repeated in-process creates; if flat, cache miss cost is bounded to first compile per process. Check whether MIGRAPHX_* env vars are honored (child-process env only, no system change).

title: AMDGPU ep-device candidate[0] fails with HIP 101 invalid device ordinal (GPU=0)
head: 2724c4cd
exception: [ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : HIP failure 101: invalid device ordinal; GPU=0; file=C:\j\amdgpu-ep\src\shared\hip\allocator.cc; line=14; expr=hipSetDevice(device_id)
impact: Candidate[0] unusable for every model; harness works around via fail-closed candidate loop (never a silent skip). GPU work happens on candidate[1]. Root cause is inside the closed vendor DLL — external boundary.
observation: With 2 AMDGPU OrtEpDevices enumerated (global indices 3 and 4 of 5), session creation on candidate[0] deterministically raises HIP 101 at hipSetDevice(device_id=0) inside the vendor EP; candidate[1] succeeds and profiles AMDGPU compute. Reproduced live 2026-11-17T21:49Z (canary) and consistent with G1-era behavior (dev[0] HIP 101, dev[1] OK).
hypotheses: The two OrtEpDevices both target the single physical iGPU but the EP assigns HIP ordinals 0/1; ordinal 0 is invalid in this driver+EP combination (only ordinal 1 backed), i.e. EP enumeration bug
Ordinal space is offset by the other 3 non-AMDGPU ep-devices; candidate index != HIP device id and cand[0] maps to a nonexistent id
GameViewer virtual display reorders/offsets device enumeration
next_discriminating_experiment: Independent short-lived processes x3: enumerate ep devices, attempt cand[0] then cand[1], record HIP error text GPU=n per candidate. If GPU=0 always for cand[0] and GPU=1 for cand[1] => enumeration-offset hypothesis strengthened; then try reversing device order to check ordinal assignment stability.

title: Dual AMDGPU ep-device enumeration indistinguishable; legacy receipts stored DXGI-0 LUID not the bound ep-device
head: 2724c4cd
impact: Identity claims in legacy receipts must be downgraded to EP_DEVICE_SELECTED(probe-evidenced) + DXGI corroboration only; PHYSICAL_GPU_IDENTITY_CORROBORATED requires new R1-C evidence.
observation: Both AMDGPU OrtEpDevices expose IDENTICAL ep_vendor/ep_options/ep_metadata (library_path, version 0.1.0) — no LUID, ordinal, or adapter hint. Old G2/G3 receipts record session.device_luid from the DXGI adapter chosen BEFORE the probe (index 0 -> 0x0:0x11746) while the session actually bound ep-device candidate[1]; therefore the legacy device_luid field is DXGI corroboration, NOT binding evidence. Identical name/VID/DID does not prove the two DXGI LUIDs (two enumerations of the same iGPU) map 1:1 to ep-device candidates.
hypotheses: The physical 8060S is one GPU enumerated twice; ep candidates are two HAL views (one broken per RCA-003) — binding to cand[1] still lands on the only physical GPU, but this must be PROVEN, not assumed
Candidates could map to the two DXGI enumerations in unknown order
next_discriminating_experiment: R1-C: per-candidate probe in isolated processes capturing profile counts + memory telemetry; correlate with DXGI/PnP evidence; if candidates remain indistinguishable, mark IDENTITY_BINDING_UNPROVEN for candidate->LUID mapping and record selection attestation instead.

title: MIGraphX auto_save_problem_cache write fails (WindowsApps protected path)
head: eb3ba42
impact: latency only; no execution/parity failure across 32+ runs
observation: Quantified: yolo26n (640 static fp32) cold session-create takes ~186 s wall in a fresh process (probe compile ~63 s + rebuild ~123 s; model compiled twice by design), while the tiny canary MatMul graph takes 1.3 s. Consistent with per-process cold MIGraphX compilation whose problem_cache cannot persist (WindowsApps ACL). In-process second create is fast.

experiments.hypothesis: cache write failure -> cold compile each process
experiments.actual_result: 186 s cold vs 1.3 s canary; rebuild 123 s in same process

causal_inference: External root cause: MSIX 1.8.65.0 attempts problem_cache.json inside its own read-only WindowsApps directory; every process pays a full cold compile for YOLO-scale graphs. Not a correctness issue (parity allclose, task parity pass); a per-process latency cost only.
mitigation: Harness-level: benchmark separates session-create from warm inference (R1-F); no system/ACL change (forbidden). Possible future: user-level MIGRAPHX cache env var if the EP honors one (untested — child-env experiment logged as next step).
remaining_uncertainty: Whether any supported env var redirects this EP's cache.

title: AMDGPU ep-device candidate[0] fails with HIP 101 invalid device ordinal (GPU=0)
head: eb3ba42
impact: candidate[0] unusable; all executions correctly routed to candidate[1]
observation: Reproduced deterministically across independent processes on 2026-11-18 (yolo26n real-model run): candidate[0] = global ep-device index 3 -> HIP failure 101 at hipSetDevice(0); candidate[1] = global index 4 -> session OK, profiler AMDGPU nodes=1 (fused), probe + rebuilt-final both positive.

experiments.hypothesis: candidate index maps to HIP ordinal and ordinal 0 is invalid in this driver+EP

causal_inference: Isolated to the vendor EP's device-ordinal assignment: the EP enumerates two AMDGPU devices but binds ordinal 0 to a nonexistent HIP device. Root cause internal to closed DLL (amdgpu-ep.dll allocator.cc hipSetDevice); external boundary — not fixable in-repo. Harness fail-closed candidate loop is the correct mitigation and is now attested per-receipt.
mitigation: create_amdgpu_session tries candidates in order, requires probe profile AMDGPU>0, revalidates the rebuilt final session, and records the full candidate_log in every receipt.
remaining_uncertainty: Why the EP enumerates a broken ordinal-0 device at all (driver enumeration offset vs MSIX bug) — cannot be discriminated without vendor-side introspection.

title: Dual AMDGPU ep-device enumeration indistinguishable; candidate->LUID mapping unproven
head: eb3ba42
impact: Legacy G2/G3 receipts' device_luid field is DXGI corroboration only (documented errata); new receipts carry attestation.
observation: Confirmed again 2026-11-18: both AMDGPU ep-devices expose identical metadata (vendor AMD, version 0.1.0, same library), no LUID/ordinal field. R1-C resolution: receipts now record device_binding with EP_DEVICE_SELECTED + per-candidate log + probe/final profile evidence + DXGI corroboration stored SEPARATELY as dxgi_corroboration (explicitly not a candidate->LUID proof). verdicts.identity distinguishes EP_DEVICE_SELECTED from PHYSICAL_GPU_IDENTITY_CORROBORATED; the latter is not claimed because the mapping is unproven.

experiments.hypothesis: ep-device metadata cannot distinguish the two candidates
experiments.actual_result: identical; only outcome (HIP 101 vs OK) distinguishes

causal_inference: EP API limitation on build 1.8.65.0. Honest labeling adopted: EP_DEVICE_SELECTED (probe-evidenced) + DXGI corroboration of the physical GPU; candidate->LUID mapping stays IDENTITY_BINDING_UNPROVEN. This is a labeling fix, not a hardware-identity doubt: single physical 8060S is corroborated by PnP/DXGI (VID 1002 DID 1586, unique non-software AMD adapter pair with identical description).
mitigation: schema v2 device_binding contract + validator enforcement (PASS requires EP_DEVICE_SELECTED or stronger + probe>0 + final profile>0).
remaining_uncertainty: If a future EP build exposes LUIDs, upgrade to PHYSICAL_GPU_IDENTITY_CORROBORATED with direct evidence.

title: MIGraphX emits gpu::precompile_op output-buffer-mismatch warnings during yolo26n-obb (1024) compile
head: ce9f577
stderr_excerpt: output buffer does not match output for gpu::precompile_op[op=pointwise...]; [op=convolution...]; [op=pooling[mode=max...]]; [op=reshape...]
impact: None observed on this case: parity allclose, task decode consistent between CPU-ORT and AMDGPU outputs (rotated-IoU pairing re-check pending in rerun). Watch item for 1024-class graphs.
observation: During cold compile of yolo26n-obb (1024x1024) the EP logs ~24 WARN lines of this signature (probe + rebuild), listing conv/pool/pointwise/reshape ops. Not observed on the six 640/768/224 models. Execution completes; numeric parity vs CPU ORT allclose=True for output0.
hypotheses: Optimizer falls back to a non-precompiled variant for these ops (warning is informational; correctness path unaffected)
Precompiled kernels produce different buffer layouts (potential silent numeric divergence path)
next_discriminating_experiment: Compare yolo26n-obb raw output0 tensors CPU vs AMDGPU element-wise beyond allclose (max abs diff at 5e-3 threshold currently); rerun obb task parity with fixed rotated-IoU comparator and record metric deltas; if task parity passes with tight margins, downgrade to informational.

title: MIGraphX gpu::precompile_op output-buffer-mismatch warnings during yolo26n-obb compile — no numeric/task impact (evidence-supported no-change closure)
head: ef2cf48
impact: none on correctness; compile logs noisier
observation: Warnings appear on every cold compile of the 1024px OBB graph (probe + rebuild + negative-control run) and not on 224/640/768 graphs.

experiments.hypothesis: warnings are informational; execution and parity unaffected
experiments.command: obb task parity with corrected vendor-NMS decode (both EPs)
experiments.actual_result: AMDGPU+DML: 15/15 matched, rotated_iou_mean=0.99999998, angle_absdiff=4.5e-6 deg; numeric parity allclose vs CPU ORT

causal_inference: No-change closure: with the harness decoder corrected, the warning-emitting compile produces task results indistinguishable from PT (IoU 0.99999998). The warnings mark optimizer fallback for specific precompiled ops, with no measurable numeric or semantic effect on this model.
mitigation: none required; watch item for future 1024px graphs
remaining_uncertainty: Whether extreme-input cases could diverge; bounded by parity thresholds on every future run
